Road speed by segment

Bar length shows road speed in mph under the current filters. Rows follow the earliest observed stop position along the route. Dot areas represent observed trips.

How it’s calculated

Speed = 60 × Σ(distance × trip count) ÷ Σ(average travel time × trip count). Distance is in miles and travel time in minutes. We combine estimated total miles and minutes rather than averaging row speeds.

Select a borough and a route to get started.

Select a segment to highlight it across all views. Dot area = observed trips

Hourly speed vs. usual

Each cell compares hourly speed with the segment’s own all-day baseline.

The baseline uses all available months and hours for the selected weekday or all weekdays for All days. Both speeds use trip-weighted miles divided by trip-weighted minutes. Percentage difference = 100 × (hourly speed ÷ baseline speed − 1).

Monthly road speed

Each line shows a segment’s monthly road speed in mph. Points mark observed months, lines connect consecutive observed months only.

Why are some lines broken?

Each point represents a month with observations for that segment. Lines connect consecutive observed months only.

A gap means the dataset has no observations for that month, or the selected weekday and hours leave no matching observations. It does not necessarily mean the bus stopped operating. Missing months are not zero speed.

Selecting a month filters the other charts; this chart keeps all twelve months for comparison.
